Stop. Sales grew, yet this stock lost eighteen thousand crore rupees in one day.
This is Cummins India. Today, it crashed fourteen percent, on more than ten times its usual volume.
You may not know the name, but you've seen its machines. The giant generators behind hospitals, malls and data centres. Engines for trucks, trains and mines.
So what went wrong? Not sales. Revenue grew four percent, to three thousand three hundred crore.
Domestic sales grew. Exports grew. Data centres kept ordering.
So why did eighteen thousand crore disappear? Stay with me, because one word decides most results days.
Analysts expected about six hundred and twenty five crore in profit. Cummins made four hundred and sixty seven. Down twenty seven percent from last year.
Was it a one-off charge? A tax hit? No. It's something you can check yourself, in thirty seconds.
Last year, from every hundred rupees of sales, Cummins kept about twenty two rupees as operating profit. This quarter, only fifteen.
Metal and freight costs went up, and the product mix changed. Sales grew. But what it kept, shrank.
And the stock is now a third below its May high of six thousand one hundred.
So on results day, don't just ask, did sales grow? Ask, out of every hundred rupees, how much did they keep?
Save this for the next results day, and follow money in cloud. Because sometimes, sales grow, and the stock still falls.
